title: Playing Markov Games Without Observing Payoffs
abstract: arXiv:2509.00179v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Optimization under uncertainty is a fundamental problem in learning and decision-making, particularly in multi-agent systems. Previously, Feldman, Kalai, and Tennenholtz [2010] demonstrated the ability to efficiently compete in repeated symmetric two-player matrix games without observing payoffs, as long as the opponents actions are observed. In this paper, we introduce and formalize a new class of zero-sum symmetric Markov games, which extends the notion of symmetry from matrix games to the Markovian setting. We show that even without observing payoffs, a player who knows the transition dynamics and observes only the opponents sequence of actions can still compete against an adversary who may have complete knowledge of the game. translated_title: 无需观测收益的马尔可夫博弈
translated_abstract: 在不确定性下进行优化是学习与决策中的一个基本问题，在多智能体系统中尤为如此。此前，Feldman、Kalai 和 Tennenholtz [2010] 证明了在重复的对称两人矩阵博弈中，只要能够观测到对手的动作，即使不观测收益，也可以高效地与之竞争。本文引入并形式化了一类新的零和对称马尔可夫博弈，将对“对称性”的概念从矩阵博弈扩展到了马尔可夫设定中。我们证明，即使不观测收益，一个仅知晓转移动态并只观测对手动作序列的玩家，仍然可以与一个可能完全掌握博弈信息的对手进行竞争。我们在这一设定下形式化了三种不同的对称性概念，并证明在这些条件下，该学习问题可以归约为在线学习的一个实例，从而使玩家能够渐进地与对手竞争。
tldr: 本文将“不观测收益也能竞争”的结果从矩阵博弈扩展到零和对称马尔可夫博弈，证明仅凭转移动态知识和对手动作序列即可与拥有完全信息的对手竞争，并将该学习问题归约为在线学习。
en_tdlr: This paper extends payoff-free competition from symmetric matrix games to zero-sum symmetric Markov games, showing that a player who knows only the transition dynamics and observes the opponent's action sequence can compete against a fully informed adversary by reducing the learning problem to online learning.
